items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: No, first I had Jimmy Heath and Cedar Walton and Sam Jones and Mickey Roker.

ctx.x: I would say like for the first two years, I just stayed over there, but then after that, I started coming over – or maybe the first year – I started coming over each summer,

like the two months the band wasn’t working I was free to come over here and started doing things over here. Clifford Jordan and I hooked up again. We had been working together years before with Horace Silver’s group. Then, I started getting some gigs around here. No, first I had Jimmy Heath and Cedar Walton and Sam Jones and Mickey Roker. But then, Jimmy started working with the Heath Brothers, and I started calling Clifford, and that was a very great relationship. Clifford was an unsung hero as a tenor…
If you have to ask, don’t mess with it. Can’t hear it, uh-oh [laughs]. Yeah, that is a trial. I saw you working frequently with Fritz Pauer over there.

items.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: performed with Duke Pearson, Nancy Wilson and Art Farmer

ctx.x: Drummer Mickey Roker was born in Miami in 1932. He grew up in the active jazz atmosphere of Philadelphia and jammed with Jimmy Heath, Lee Morgan and McCoy Tyner. Mickey re-settled in New York in the late ‘50’s and performed with Duke Pearson, Nancy Wilson and Art Farmer, later teaming up with Joe Williams from 1961-63. Much of the ‘70’s was spent with Dizzy Gillespie, with whom he shared a love and talent for Latin music. Such musical giants as Oscar Peterson, Ray Brown and Sonny Rollins have called on Mickey to…
